title: Halves and quarters: which part is marked
objective: Identify whether a marked part of a set is one half, one quarter, or three quarters.
summary: Adults in workplace onboarding practice naming a marked part of a set as one half, one quarter, or three quarters, using rosters, parcels, and checklist steps, with adaptive support.

audience.description: Adults starting a new role who want to feel confident reading halves and quarters in everyday work counts.

skill.name: Halves and quarters of a set

prerequisites.text: Split a set into equal groups and count how many are in each group.
Count all items in a set and count a marked part of that set.

essential_facts.text: One half means the whole set split into 2 equal groups, taking 1 of those groups.
One quarter means the whole set split into 4 equal groups, taking 1 of those groups, and three quarters means taking 3 of those groups.
To identify a marked part, count the marked items, count the whole set, and work out how many equal groups the marked part covers.
The size of one equal group is the total divided by the number of groups.

contexts.label: Shift roster
contexts.scenario_template: A {{whole}} lists {{total}} {{item_plural}}. {{marked_count}} {{item_plural}} are marked as {{state}}. Which fraction of the {{item_plural}} is marked as {{state}}?
contexts.limits: Shifts differ in length and timing in a real roster; here every shift counts the same, so the fraction is about how many shifts, not how many hours.

contexts.label: Parcel delivery
contexts.scenario_template: A {{whole}} includes {{total}} {{item_plural}}. {{marked_count}} {{item_plural}} are marked as {{state}}. Which fraction of the {{item_plural}} is marked as {{state}}?
contexts.limits: Parcels differ in size and weight in real deliveries; here every parcel counts the same, so the fraction is about how many parcels, not how much space they take.

contexts.label: Onboarding checklist
contexts.scenario_template: An onboarding {{whole}} has {{total}} {{item_plural}}. {{marked_count}} {{item_plural}} are marked as {{state}}. Which fraction of the {{item_plural}} is marked as {{state}}?
contexts.limits: Checklist steps differ in effort in real onboarding; here every step counts the same, so the fraction is about how many steps, not how long onboarding takes.

confusions.description: Chooses the fraction for the part that is not marked instead of the marked part.
Uses the right number of equal parts but the wrong number of them taken, for example naming two quarters where the marked part covers a different number of quarters.
Chooses a fraction with a different grouping of the whole, so it does not describe the marked part at all.

essential.title: The key idea
essential.body_template: The marked part is {{part_size}} of {{total}} {{item_plural}}. Split {{total}} into {{denominator}} equal groups of {{group_size}}. The marked part takes {{numerator}} of those groups, so it is {{fraction_text}} ({{fraction_symbol}}).

worked-example.title: Worked example
worked-example.body_template: Here is one worked through. The {{whole}} has {{total}} {{item_plural}}, and {{part_size}} are marked as {{state}}. That marked part is {{fraction_text}} of the whole set.
steps_template: Split {{total}} into {{group_count}} equal groups: {{total}} divided by {{group_count}} gives {{group_size}} in each group.
Count how many groups are marked: {{part_size}} divided by {{group_size}} gives {{numerator}}.
So the marked part is {{fraction_text}} ({{fraction_symbol}}) of the {{item_plural}}.

contrast.title: Which part is marked
contrast.body_template: Compare the marked and unmarked parts. The marked part is {{part_size}} {{item_plural}}, which is {{fraction_text}} of {{total}}. The part that is not marked is {{remaining}} {{item_plural}}. Choose the fraction for the marked part, not the part that is left.

hints: Start from the whole: there are {{total}} {{item_plural}} in the {{whole}}.
Count the marked {{item_plural}}. Split {{total}} into equal groups and work out how many {{item_plural}} are in one group.
One equal group is {{group_size}} {{item_plural}}. The marked part covers {{numerator}} of {{denominator}} groups, which is {{fraction_text}}.

must: Speak to an adult, plainly and respectfully.
Describe what happened in the task, never what the person is.

tests.name: five of twenty marked is one quarter
eighteen of twenty four marked is three quarters
two of four counts as one half
two of eight counts as one quarter
three quarters chosen for a one quarter marked part
two quarters chosen for a three quarters marked part
